concerns.text: FR-13 cites '(See US-03 AC5)' but US-03 has only four acceptance criteria (AC1-AC4). Stale cross-reference; either add an AC5 to US-03 or correct the citation.

SC-001 states US-01 is successful 'when FR-001 - FR-009 are satisfied', but FR-005 (stratification), FR-006 (three annotators), and FR-007 (Cohen's Kappa) are US-02 requirements with no role in US-01's acceptance criteria. This contradicts SC-002, which correctly scopes US-02 to FR-006-FR-009/FR-015, and silently widens US-01's scope. SC-001 should reference FR-001-FR-004 (and FR-008's statistical thresholds) only.

FR-007 requires 'overall agreement must be κ ≥ 0.6' with three annotators but does not state how Kappa is aggregated across three raters (pairwise mean, Fleiss' Kappa, or majority-label vs each rater). The threshold is measurable, but the measurement procedure is ambiguous — an implementer cannot know which statistic to compute. Specify the aggregation (e.g., mean pairwise Cohen's Kappa or Fleiss' Kappa).

The chi-squared test's testability depends on expected cell counts, which depend on the [deferred] stratification quantile. The idea already fixes top-20%/bottom-20%; the spec should either adopt that value or state the minimum bin size / expected-count condition so the test procedure is reproducible. As written, the metric and reference are named, so this is a phrasing fix, not a missing requirement.

The idea explicitly specifies stratification quantiles: 'top 20%' and 'bottom 20%' drift bins. The spec replaces these with '[deferred]' ('top [deferred] of drift_score'). The [deferred] convention covers unverified EMPIRICAL values; the 20% cut is a stated design parameter from the source idea, not a measured quantity, so deferring it silently drops an idea-mandated requirement. Restore the 20%/20% quantiles (or justify a different fixed value).

Human annotation is restricted to the top/bottom [deferred] drift bins, but FR-009 (logistic regression, AUC-ROC) and FR-010 (Flan-T5 AUC) are evaluated on this annotated set. Range restriction to the extremes of drift_score biases the regression coefficient, AUC, and Cohen's d (separation of extremes is near-guaranteed by construction). Either annotate a random sample of the full drift range, or restrict AUC/comparison claims to the binned subset and state the limitation.

Three annotators label 'novel attack'/'known attack'/'benign', but the spec never defines how the three-way labels are aggregated into the binary 'novel' gold standard used by FR-008/FR-009/FR-010 (majority vote? unanimity? how are 'known attack' logs treated — excluded or folded into benign?). The gold-standard construction rule must be specified, since it determines every downstream statistic.

Cohen's d ≥ 0.5 is paired with a Mann-Whitney U test. Cohen's d assumes approximately normal distributions; with a nonparametric test a rank-based effect size (e.g., rank-biserial or Cliff's delta) is more consistent. Specify which effect size and how d is computed (pooled SD) if retained.

The review_flag threshold drift_score ≥ 0.5 is asserted with no calibration rationale (cosine-distance scale depends on embedding geometry). State that it is a pre-registered operating point, or tie it to a quantile of the score distribution, so it is not confused with a validated decision boundary.

new_concerns.text: The chi-squared test's testability depends on expected cell counts, which depend on the stratification quantile. The reviser stated that [deferred] was replaced with '20%', but the artifact still contains '[deferred]' in US-02 AC1 and FR-005. This must be explicitly set to 20% to ensure the test procedure is reproducible.

Prior concern scope-056605df remains unresolved. Despite the reviser's claim that 20% quantiles were restored, US-02 AC1 and FR-005 still use '[deferred]' markers ('top [deferred] of drift_score'). These are design parameters from the idea, not empirical values, and must be explicitly stated as 20%.
